rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for the beginning of an activity.

example.english: The start of the event is at nine in the morning.
example.traditional: 個活動嘅開始係朝早九點。
example.jyutping: go3 wut6 dung6 ge3 hoi1 ci2 hai6 ziu1 zou2 gau2 dim2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for beginning or initiating something, including saying where something begins.

example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 baat3 dim2 hoi1 ci2 soeng5 tong4

rows.note: Use 起點 when “start” means a marked point in a race, route, or game.

example.english: This is the start of the race track.
example.jyutping: ni1 dou6 hai6 tiu4 coi3 dou6 ge3 hei2 dim2

rows.note: Use this for starting a machine, appliance, or electronic device rather than a vehicle engine.

example.english: You start the computer first, and I’ll make tea.
example.jyutping: nei5 hoi1 gei1 sin1 ngo5 heoi3 zam1 caa4

rows.note: Use this specifically for starting a vehicle or its engine, rather than an ordinary machine.

example.jyutping: gaa3 ce1 zung6 mei6 zoek6 ce1

rows.note: Use 一驚 for the brief involuntary jerk or fright caused by surprise.

example.english: They suddenly tapped my shoulder and made me start.
example.traditional: 佢突然拍我膊頭，搞到我一驚。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dat6 jin4 paak3 ngo5 bok3 tau4 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 jat1 geng1

rows.note: Use this colloquial expression when someone begins menstruating, rather than the general verb 開始.

example.english: I think my period will start today.
example.jyutping: ngo5 nam2 gam1 jat6 wui5 lai4 ging1

rows.note: Use 著數 when the advantage comes from being allowed to begin earlier.

example.english: We leave ten minutes early, so we already have a head start.
example.traditional: 我哋早十分鐘出發，已經有著數。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 zou2 sap6 fan1 zung1 ceot1 faat3 ji5 ging1 jau5 zoek6 sou3
